title: Arm serving thread-efficiency profile
scope: Quality-gated server CPU-time right-sizing on the promoted repack-on f16/256/64 cached single-slot native Arm service
hypothesis: Three or two inference threads can reduce measured-window llama-server CPU seconds per request by at least 5 percent while retaining at least 95 percent of four-thread throughput, preserving median and p95 HTTP latency within 5 percent, and reproducing every selected E3f prediction.
measurement_boundary: Linux process user and system CPU counters are sampled from /proc/<llama-server-pid>/stat after both warmups and immediately around the 30 measured requests. Model load, readiness, warmups, the Python client, and post-measurement shutdown are excluded. CPU time is not an energy or power measurement.

prior_evidence.selected_service: E5f promoted a 64/64 prompt batch; E5e promoted f16 K/V cache and a 256-token context; E5i retained automatic Flash Attention as the configured default; repacked weights, shared-prefix caching, and one slot remain enabled.

runtime_source.mechanism: The Pareto64 launch recipe binds both llama.cpp --threads and --threads-batch to the selected profile. Each measured probe independently binds the sampled Linux PID to the live llama-server child and derives CPU seconds from monotonically increasing utime and stime counters using the host clock tick rate.
runtime_source.declared_risk: Lower thread counts can reduce scheduling work yet lengthen each request. CPU-time reduction, throughput, tail latency, exact answers, and prefix reuse are therefore independent measured obligations. CPU seconds do not establish energy savings without power data.

selection_policy.eligible_profiles: A lower-thread profile must pass every quality, prefix-reuse, throughput, latency, process CPU-time, readiness, and RSS gate.
tie_breakers: lower repeated median server CPU seconds per request
selection_policy.no_win_rule: Keep four threads when no candidate clears every frozen gate; retain the complete negative result without changing thresholds.
